column4: The section's watering-place departure is stated almost verbatim: people يَصْدُرُ ... أَشْتَاتًا on the Day their deeds are shown, turning scattered motion into the disclosure of divergent effort.
The section defines every good or evil deed as sa'y; this ayah makes مَا سَعَىٰ the only effort a human can claim, fixing responsibility to each runner's chosen course.
The runner's effort will be seen, وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ, so the divergent courses of 92:4 do not remain hidden at the finish.
This ayah gives the preceding seen effort its full recompense, completing the section's movement from sa'y through judgment to final satisfaction.
The ayah joins distinct ways, a command to race in good deeds, common return to God, and disclosure of اختلاف; it gathers the section's directions, race, finish, and revealed difference in one scene.
One who aims at the immediate life is sped toward what God allots and then toward Hell, a precise instance of a runner being carried along the chosen bad direction.
One who aims at the Hereafter and سَعَىٰ لَهَا سَعْيَهَا has that effort thanked, directly joining intention, proper running, and the good finish.
God says كُلًّا نُمِدُّ, extending provision to both groups named in 17:18-19; this clarifies how divine enabling can accompany opposite human directions.
وَلِكُلٍّ وِجْهَةٌ names each runner's direction, مُوَلِّيهَا names the turning, and فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ converts direction into a commanded race.
وَعَلَى اللَّهِ قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ directly matches the section's “upon Us is guidance,” while وَمِنْهَا جَائِرٌ sets the straight-directed road against a deviating one.
وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ is the Quran's explicit pair of shown high roads, the closest external statement of the section's two-way image.
وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ repeats both the divine promise and the y-s-r wording of 92:7, making the Messenger the addressed runner whose course is prepared.
فَلِلَّهِ الْآخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَىٰ is the direct verbal counterpart of 92:13 and places both temporal ends of the race under God's ownership.
This ayah joins the boundary لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُدَاهُمْ, God's guidance, spending solely for وَجْهِ اللَّهِ, and full repayment, matching the good runner's direction, gift, motive, and finish.
أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنَىٰ opens a branch with the same self-sufficiency that marks the withholding course in surah 92.
وَأَمَّا مَن جَاءَكَ يَسْعَىٰ combines the branching frame with purposeful swift approach, staging the section's physical and moral sa'y together.
The approaching runner is وَهُوَ يَخْشَىٰ, so fear identifies the inward direction of the outward sa'y just as taqwa distinguishes the good course in surah 92.
On the Day of disclosure, the human remembers مَا سَعَىٰ; the runner's whole course becomes present at its finish.
فَأَمَّا مَن طَغَىٰ opens the first of the same two grammatical and moral branches developed in the section.
وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ opens the opposite branch and grounds its direction in fear of standing before God.
لِسَعْيِهَا رَاضِيَةٌ explicitly makes faces pleased with their sa'y, joining the section's first action word to its final promised satisfaction.
سَابِقُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ commands a race toward forgiveness and Garden, supplying the good course with an explicit finish line.
وَالسَّابِقُونَ السَّابِقُونَ names the racers who have passed ahead, directly activating the section's secondary competitive sense of sa'y.
The section's usr-path becomes يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ at its eschatological end, so difficulty names both course and arriving day.
عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ denies ease to the unbelievers on that difficult day, exposing the limit of the bad road's apparent ease while it is being traveled.
تَحْسَبُهُمْ جَمِيعًا وَقُلُوبُهُمْ شَتَّىٰ makes the section's opened seam inward: visible togetherness can conceal truly scattered hearts.
يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَفَرَّقُونَ gives the other explicit Resurrection-day separation named by the section, when a formerly common company breaks into final groups.
كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلَىٰ شَاكِلَتِهِ states that each acts from a distinct disposition, while أَهْدَىٰ سَبِيلًا judges which resulting course is better directed.
Every human is كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ and will meet Him, an exact nonlexical picture of all effort as motion toward an unavoidable finish.
The right-handed runner receives حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا, making ease an attribute of the good course's reckoning and arrival.
The one easily reckoned returns to his people joyful, providing the good route's homecoming and satisfaction.
Receiving the record behind the back begins the opposing route, using bodily orientation to mark the reversed course.
The bad-route traveler calls for destruction, the realized end of a course that had seemed traversable.
وَيَصْلَىٰ سَعِيرًا supplies the fire at the end of the opposing route, completing the parallel with surah 92's warning.
فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ depicts the good way as a steep ascent that must be broken through, correcting the impression that the truly easy end must feel easiest at the start.
Freeing a neck is the first concrete act on the steep road, giving the shown high way an ethically costly direction.
Feeding on a day of hunger continues the road as giving under difficulty, directly paralleling the giver's course in surah 92.
The orphan of near kin identifies one recipient of the steep-road gift, making the runner's generosity concrete.
The destitute in dust completes the giving scene and shows why the good road can be arduous before its ease.
أَصْحَابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ names the company reached by those acts, turning the route into a final side and group.
Those who reject the signs become أَصْحَابُ الْمَشْأَمَةِ, the opposing final company formed by the other direction.
عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ مُؤْصَدَةٌ closes the bad high road with an enclosing fire, matching surah 92's terminal warning.
إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ presents one shown road followed by the alternatives شَاكِرًا and كَفُورًا, the same guidance-before-division relation as the section.
Chains and Blaze state the destination prepared for the ungrateful branch of 76:3, giving that response its road-end.
The righteous fulfill vows and fear the spreading Day, joining committed action and fear on the thankful route.
They give food despite loving it to the needy, orphan, and captive, concretizing the giving course that surah 92 sketches.
لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ and the refusal of جَزَاءً وَلَا شُكُورًا directly match giving solely for the Lord's face without seeking repayment.
Their fear of a grim Day explains the direction behind the gift and ties the earthly act to its difficult or easy finish.
سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَن يَخْشَىٰ shows the fearing hearer taking the reminder, the receptive branch after the promise of facilitation in 87:8.
وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَى names the opposing wretched branch that avoids the reminder, paralleling surah 92's two persons.
The wretched one enters الْنَّارَ الْكُبْرَىٰ, giving the avoided reminder's course its fiery destination.
لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ makes the endpoint a suspension between death and life, revealing the extremity concealed by the apparently easy wrong course.
قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ links purification to success, directly matching the giver who gives wealth يَتَزَكَّىٰ in surah 92.
بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا identifies preference for the nearer life as the choice that bends effort toward the wrong end.
وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ supplies the evaluative difference between the two temporal ends owned by God in 92:13.
وَلَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَّكَ مِنَ الْأُولَىٰ uses the same two end-terms and ranks the later one above the first for the addressed Messenger.
وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ joins divine giving to future satisfaction, closely echoing the promised pleasure at the section's finish.
People emerge from graves سِرَاعًا كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ, a Resurrection race toward visible goal-markers that turns the section's metaphor into a final scene.
The earth splits, people emerge سِرَاعًا, and God calls that gathering عَلَيْنَا يَسِيرٌ; swift motion and divine ease meet at Resurrection.
From the graves إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَنسِلُونَ stages rapid common departure toward the Lord, the final version of runners leaving one point for a goal.
People become كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ, a bodily image of the same final dispersal conveyed by أشتات at the watering place.
The Day of Gathering resolves into فَرِيقٌ فِي الْجَنَّةِ وَفَرِيقٌ فِي السَّعِيرِ, making two final companies out of one assembly.
Those who disbelieved are driven to Hell زُمَرًا, a procession in groups along the bad route to its gate.
Those who feared their Lord are driven to the Garden زُمَرًا, the corresponding procession of groups along the opposite route.
وَكُنتُمْ أَزْوَاجًا ثَلَاثَةً explicitly turns humanity into three final kinds, extending the section's separation image beyond a simple pair.
The companions of the right are the first named company after the threefold division, locating one finish-side.
The companions of the left are the opposed company after the division, locating the contrary finish-side.
أُولَٰئِكَ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ supplies the destination of the forerunners named in 56:10: passing ahead ends in nearness.
At the arriving Day, humanity divides into شَقِيٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ, making final wretchedness and happiness the revealed forms of divergent courses.
Those made wretched are in the Fire, giving one class named in 11:105 its destination.
Those made happy are in the Garden, giving the opposed class its enduring destination.
The Godfearing are gathered to the Merciful وَفْدًا, a dignified procession at the end of their directed course.
The criminals are driven to Hell وِرْدًا, a thirsty counter-procession that recalls the section's watering-place departure while reversing its destination.
God's straight path is singular, while following السُّبُلَ makes people تَفَرَّقَ بِكُمْ from it; the ayah explicitly joins road choice to dispersal.
The ayah contrasts one walking fallen on his face with one walking سَوِيًّا عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ, making bodily gait reveal which course is truly guided.
Those who strive toward God are answered لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا, directly linking exertion with divine guidance into roads.
Whoever turns blindly from the Reminder is assigned a devil companion, showing a wrong orientation being furnished with its own escort.
The companions bar them from السَّبِيل while they يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ, precisely exposing the bad road that feels right to its runner.
Arrival before God reveals the companion's true distance, so unnoticed misdirection becomes visible only at the finish.
The question about the greatest losers in deeds prepares a judgment of effort by destination rather than by the runner's confidence.
ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ describes effort itself going astray in the nearer life while its runners think they do good, the section's unnoticed acceleration down the wrong way.
One group is guided and the other deserves error after taking devils as allies while thinking themselves guided, a direct two-group version of deceptive directional ease.
One whose evil work is beautified sees it as good; this is the inward mechanism by which the hard destination can feel like an easy road.
Satan beautifies past peoples' deeds and bars them from السَّبِيل despite their perceptiveness, another explicit case of capable runners diverted without recognizing the course.
نُوَلِّهِ مَا تَوَلَّىٰ states that God turns the dissenter toward what he chose, then brings him to Hell; it closely matches facilitation in the runner's selected direction.
Those who prefer the nearer life and seek God's way عِوَجًا combine temporal preference with making the road crooked, the section's twisted usr-course stated directly.
فَاهْدُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ الْجَحِيمِ uses guidance language for conveyance to Hell, a stark reversal that makes destination essential to judging guidance.
The soul is inspired with both its depravity and its fear, placing the two moral directions before the runner internally.
Success belongs to the one who purifies the soul, matching the good runner whose gift is made يَتَزَكَّىٰ.
Failure belongs to the one who buries the soul, completing the opposed direction to purification and success.
The jinn divide themselves into submitters and deviators, and the submitters تَحَرَّوْا رَشَدًا, deliberately seeking the right direction.
The deviators become fuel for Hell, supplying the other self-described group with its finish.
The Hour comes so every soul may be repaid بِمَا تَسْعَىٰ, directly making sa'y the measured substance of final recompense.
The believer who does righteous deeds finds لَا كُفْرَانَ لِسَعْيِهِ and the effort written, securing the good runner's work against loss.
Punishment is placed upon مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ, exactly reproducing the paired denial and turning-away that identify surah 92's bad runner.
وَلَٰكِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ repeats the exact two acts of 92:16, confirming that rejection is simultaneously a turn in direction.
إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ again makes denial and turning away one coordinated motion, a direct lexical counterpart to the section's bad course.
إِلَّا مَن تَوَلَّىٰ وَكَفَرَ gives the same identifying turn and disbelief in reversed order, beside the surah that names satisfaction with sa'y.
أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ introduces a runner defined by turning away, directly recalling the section's directional reading of tawallā.
وَأَعْطَىٰ قَلِيلًا وَأَكْدَىٰ shows giving that stops short, a precise boundary against the sustained giving course of surah 92.
مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّي مَالِيَهْ is the speaker's final realization of 92:11: wealth does not avail at the fall and finish.
مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ closely repeats the section's claim that accumulated wealth cannot rescue its owner from the fiery end.
يَوْمَ لَا يَنفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ generalizes the section's failed wealth to the Day when neither wealth nor children benefit.
Wealth and children will not avail the unbelievers before God, and the ayah names them as fuel of the Fire, joining failed means to destination.
Neither wealth nor children avail against God, and those who relied on them become companions of the Fire, another direct boundary on the bad runner's resources.
Charity is taken مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ to purify and تزكيهم, directly unpacking how giving wealth can be the act of self-purification in 92:18.
Giving zakat while seeking وَجْهَ اللَّهِ joins gift, pure direction, and increase, closely matching the motive and result of 92:18-20.
السَّابِقُونَ الْأَوَّلُونَ combines the racers who pass ahead with the “first” root, then ends with reciprocal divine pleasure, uniting the section's race, order, and satisfaction.
Those who يُؤْتُونَ مَا آتَوا give while their hearts fear return to their Lord, joining gift, fear, and the anticipated finish.
أُولَٰئِكَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ وَهُمْ لَهَا سَابِقُونَ explicitly turns the fearful givers of 23:60 into racers and forerunners.
One inherited Book yields a self-wronger, a moderate person, and one سَابِقٌ بِالْخَيْرَاتِ, a direct picture of disparate efforts emerging from a shared gift.
وَفِي ذَٰلِكَ فَلْيَتَنَافَسِ الْمُتَنَافِسُونَ commands competition for the righteous reward just described, supplying a clearly named object for the race.
وَسَارِعُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ directs rapid movement toward forgiveness and Garden, another explicit good-course command with destination.
فَاسْعَوْا إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ uses sa'y as commanded purposeful quick movement toward a named goal, grounding the section's physical dictionary sense.
After common prayer, فَانتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ sends people dispersing into the land to seek God's bounty, a close enacted analogue to departure from a shared stopping place.
The nearer life is a brief, competitive display that becomes dry debris; this tells the runners what passes before 57:21 commands the race toward what remains.
One who wants the harvest of the Hereafter has it increased, while one who wants the worldly harvest receives some but no share later, a complete pair of intended directions and apportioned ends.
Those who desire the nearer life receive their works there in full, showing a chosen direction provisionally paid along its own course.
The same worldly-directed group has only Fire in the Hereafter and its deeds fail, revealing the course's actual terminal difficulty.
Thamud are guided but فَاسْتَحَبُّوا الْعَمَىٰ عَلَى الْهُدَىٰ, making the wrong route a preference exercised after direction is shown.
لَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي الْأُولَىٰ وَالْآخِرَةِ places both first and later under God and adds judgment and return, matching the race's two temporal bounds and judge.
إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ contrasts the Messenger's limit with God's act of guiding, clarifying who bears the “upon Us” statement in 92:12.
وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِي إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ gives the Messenger a real derivative role of directing to God's straight path, complementing rather than erasing divine guidance.
اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ is the worshipper's direct request that God set the direction toward the straight road imagined in the section.
The requested path is distinguished from the courses of غضب and ضلال, so guidance is completed by identifying divergent ends to avoid.
Whoever follows God's guidance neither strays nor suffers, a divine statement joining the shown direction to the character of its route.
Whoever turns away from God's reminder receives a constricted life and blind resurrection, giving the opposite orientation its hard end.
God opens the breast of the one guided and makes the breast of the one led astray tight كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي السَّمَاءِ, rendering opposed guidance as bodily ease and arduous ascent.
Those already guided receive increased guidance and taqwa, showing divine preparation intensifying the direction a runner has taken.
The Merciful extends the one in error further until the promised end is seen, a close parallel to allowing a wrong-directed runner to proceed easily toward disclosure.
وَيَزِيدُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا هُدًى gives the opposing increase to those guided, forming with 19:75 two divinely extended directions.
People emerge from graves كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرَادٌ مُّنتَشِرٌ, another concrete Resurrection image of a common multitude becoming spread out.
They hurry toward the caller while unbelievers say هَٰذَا يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌ, joining rapid final motion to the difficult day at its end.
A man comes مِنْ أَقْصَى الْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ to warn Moses, embodying sa'y as swift purposeful travel from a distant point.
A man likewise comes مِنْ أَقْصَى الْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ to direct his people toward the messengers, joining literal running with urgent guidance.
On the final Day the believers' light يَسْعَىٰ before and beside them toward good news of Gardens, giving sa'y a luminous motion at the good finish.
The believers' light يَسْعَىٰ before them as they ask God to perfect it, staging directed final motion together with dependence on divine completion.
ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعَىٰ makes Pharaoh's sa'y a running away after he turns his back, a precise negative form of the section's purposeful race.
Moses is warned not to be turned from the Hour by one following desire فَتَرْدَىٰ; the same r-d-y root makes diversion end in ruin.
People come to God فُرَادَىٰ and leave behind what was granted them, joining solitary arrival to the failure of possessions at the finish.
God is pleased with the Garden's people and they with Him, and the ayah grounds that end in fear of the Lord, matching fear-directed effort ending in pleasure.
ارْجِعِي إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً is a direct homeward finish in reciprocal satisfaction, the destination implied by 92:21.
فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا puts ease with hardship rather than assigning them to separate routes, a boundary on reading yusr and usr as permanently isolated domains.
The repeated promise that ease accompanies hardship confirms that felt difficulty within the good route need not identify the bad destination.
سَيَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا makes God bring ease after hardship, reversing the section's spatial two-road picture into a temporal transformation.
اعْتَصِمُوا ... جَمِيعًا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا commands maintained joining and recalls God joining hostile hearts, the positive opposite of the section's opened seam.
أَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ makes divine joining of hearts the exact relational opposite of hearts that are shattā and groups whose adhesion has lifted.
The command not to be like those who تَفَرَّقُوا after clear signs identifies blameworthy division as a preventable reversal of communal cohesion.
Those who obstruct God's way and seek it عِوَجًا turn a straight-directed road into a crooked one, clarifying the image's iltiwā' by explicit opposition.
The same obstruction and search for عِوَجًا is tied to denial of the Hereafter, connecting crookedness of course to rejection of its finish.
A devil appointed as ally will mislead its follower and يَهْدِيهِ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ السَّعِيرِ; “guiding” to Blaze is the dark reversal of guidance to the good end.
God's covenant not to worship Satan identifies an alternative leader on the road and calls him an evident enemy.
وَأَنِ اعْبُدُونِي هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ sets the straight route of worship directly against the satanic course prohibited in 36:60.
Those content and satisfied with the nearer life reverse the section's final satisfaction: their riḍā attaches to the passing start rather than the lasting finish.
Fire becomes the refuge earned by that misplaced satisfaction, exposing its terminal reversal.

The source-section root sense makes sa'y a race, while بَلَغَ مَعَهُ السَّعْيَ names the son's reaching the capacity for shared labor; it shows sa'y can also join two workers rather than scatter them.
At the struck rock كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ: groups know distinct drinking places before they depart, a structured division at water rather than the section's dispersal after one watering point.
Twelve tribes and twelve springs again organize each group around its known drinking place, illuminating a Quranic boundary to the section's single-source departure image.
After the separation of 30:14, believers who did good are delighted in a meadow, so this row supplies one separated group's own destination.
After the same separation, deniers are brought to punishment, supplying the other group's destination.
Hell is made visible to whoever sees immediately before the two branches, placing the bad destination at the race's line of sight.
The transgressor يُؤْثِرُ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا, identifying preference for the first life as the motive of the first branch.
فَإِنَّ الْجَحِيمَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَىٰ gives the worldly-preferring branch its final lodging.
فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَىٰ gives the fearing and self-restraining branch its opposed lodging.
The addressee attends to the self-sufficient person, showing how human attention can follow the wrong status-marker even when the two inner directions differ.
The addressee is distracted from the fearful runner, completing the scene's reversal between outward prestige and inward direction.
Receiving the book in the right hand identifies the traveler who then receives the easy reckoning of 84:8.
The question وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْعَقَبَةُ pauses over the uphill road and prepares its deeds as the explanation of what traversing it means.
Faith, mutual patience, and mercy bind the preceding gifts into a sustained communal course rather than an isolated donation.
The righteous drink from a cup at the good branch's destination, supplying a concrete reward before their deeds are recalled.
The spring made to gush by God's servants extends that destination scene and contrasts with the thirsty procession to Hell in 19:86.
The command to remind follows the promise of facilitation, showing a human act through which divine road-preparation reaches hearers.
Remembering the Lord's name and praying supplies the purified person's positive practice before the worldly/Hereafter contrast.
